why_this_fixture: The most discriminating of the seven: it is the core in-session contract, so an invoke agent reading prose that predates the seam cannot answer it correctly by accident. The negative control 01 is deliberately NOT used here - it would pass against the old prose, which is what makes it a control rather than a discriminator.
note_on_prose_set: references/external-executor.md and references/correction-continuation.md do not exist at 3e3a2f3; their absence is the change under test.

result.notes: The output denies that an external-executor mode exists at all - it refuses the flag, never builds an external_execution_request or invokes the caller-supplied procedure, and drives the ordinary nested ossify:implementer-agent path instead (mode_split); it treats the caller's whole-round capability as a violation of decomposition order rather than preserving ordering across the seam (round_sequencing); it requires only the two ordinary return shapes with no *_oid fields and has close consume report_path/stage_status verbatim, exactly the trust-the-declared-values failure the fixture falsifies, with no recomputed four-part identity check against the request (result_validation); it never routes a gaps record through the section 6 loop as a replacement single-item request through the caller and instead prescribes re-dispatch to ossify:implementer-agent (gaps_routing); and it says nothing about a same-executor correction continuation or inline Layer 4, while its re-dispatch instruction contradicts the same-executor rule (correction_and_layer4).

verdict: DETECTS - control failed as required. Scores are at or below the round-three run on every criterion (1/2/1/2/2 against 1/1/1/2/2): the old prose has no notion of the seam at all, so criterion 4's new branch-identity clause cannot make it any weaker than it already was.
